text: {"rules":[{"id":"ASPIRIN-PREECLAMPSIA-PREG","version":"September 2021","title":"Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks of gestation for pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia","source_quote":"The USPSTF recommends the use of low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) as preventive medication after 12 weeks of gestation in persons who are at high risk for preeclampsia.","grade":"B","effective_date":"2021-09","action":"Recommend low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) as preventive medication after 12 weeks of gestation in pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia.","denominator":"{\"all\": [{\"condition\": {\"concept\": \"pregnancy\"}, \"quote\": \"pregnant persons\"}, {\"uncomputable\": {\"needs\": \"clinical determination that the pregnant person is at high risk for preeclampsia (risk factors defined in Practice Considerations, not in this section)\"}, \"quote\": \"persons who are at high risk for preeclampsia\"}, {\"uncomputable\": {\"needs\": \"current gestational age greater than 12 weeks\"}, \"quote\": \"after 12 weeks of gestation\"}], \"quote\": \"pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia\"}","numerator":"{\"uncomputable\": {\"needs\": \"record of low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) use as preventive medication; the criterion grammar has no medication type\"}, \"quote\": \"low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day)\"}","exclusions":"[]"}],"coverage_notes":["Definition of 'high risk for preeclampsia' is deferred to the Practice Considerations section, which is not included in this section text; encoded as uncomputable rather than approximated with computable conditions.","Gestational age (after 12 weeks of gestation) is not a concept in the vocabulary and was encoded as uncomputable.","Numerator (low-dose aspirin use) is encoded as uncomputable: the criterion grammar has no medication type and the vocabulary has no aspirin concept. A new concept such as 'low_dose_aspirin' would be needed to make it computable.","Aspirin dose details beyond 81 mg/day, timing of initiation and duration (e.g., continuation until delivery) are referenced to Practice Considerations and not represented.","The asterisk after the date ('September 2021 *') is unexplained in this section and was not represented."]}
